clue.text: Soldier returning in ceremonial clothing to introduce, irrelevant matter

parts.note: formal dress is ceremonial clothing, as in full dress uniform

indicators.note: returning says the soldier word is read backwards, coming back the way it went

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home in his dress uniform is asked to bring up something beside the point.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is US Army slang for a soldier; 'returning' and 'in' are the two indicators. The comma is surface punctuation: the definition runs from 'to introduce' to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off the subject is to bring in matter that does not bear on it.

parts.note: the discus is thrown in athletics

clue.text: Small worker should get things down quickly

clue.text: Place where one may be found in speech

definitions.text: Place where one may be found

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person can be tracked down by what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Your home or postal location is where you are found; a formal speech to an audience is the other sense.

clue.text: Underwear for one team-leader

explanation.definitionFit: A sniff, as a noun, is a smell or whiff picked up by the nose.

explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's procedure on a patient is called an operation.

clue.text: Not suitable to be incompetent

explanation.surface: Being unfit for a job means being useless at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not altered to suit a purpose is unfit for it; an incompetent person is likewise unfit for the task.

clue.text: Pole leaving hostel for other accommodation

parts.note: S, for south, is one of the Earth's poles

clue.text: Rigid as a body may be

explanation.surface: Stiff as a corpse might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending; in slang a corpse, a dead body, is called a stiff.

clue.text: Self-employed person has fish in France

indicators.note: in says the fish word sits inside France

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End.

clue.text: Railway locomotive's position for an imposter

explanation.definitionFit: The engine stands before the coal wagon behind it; a fraud laying a false claim to a title is a claimant of that sort.

clue.text: Render for each around the end

clue.text: Stick pole in head

clue.text: Beg for a bit of golden treatment

clue.text: Very good lot of dollars

clue.text: Make proud Oriental tardy
